steps.text: In *The remote passed pawn: bring the king first* you learned to move the king before the far pawn runs. Now the positions come unlabeled: sometimes pushing the passer is the move, sometimes the king must go first. Ask what each king can reach while the pawn runs, then choose. Decide the next position.

Look at what the king move did. After Kf5, Black is to move and all five legal Black moves lose, because Kxe5 follows whatever Black plays. This is not zugzwang: Black would lose even if it could pass. The king move wins because it attacks e5 and Black cannot defend it. Predict the result for the side to move.

**Rule of thumb:** hold the passer back while your king has work to do, and push it when the push gains ground at once. Often the king's distance decides [I]: the next three positions show one case. Predict the three positions.

steps.title: The king's distance
steps.prompt: Black to move in each. In the second position only the black king has moved, one file to the right; in the third only the white king has moved. Predict win, draw or loss for Black.
Before each answer: did you ask which king reaches the pawns first, or did you push because the pawn was passed? Write the question you will ask first next time.
